scenarios.title: Repair an SMB login and its Unix access
scenarios.summary: Restore the supplied SMB accounts and the folder access needed by two team members.
scenarios.objective: Enable the supplied test SMB accounts for mira and noor; their Unix identities and groups already exist. Let both team members list /srv/team-reports and reach its existing files. The writer must read and replace draft.txt; the reviewer must read checklist.txt and be denied writes by share policy. Keep casey and anonymous clients out of the team share. Preserve every supplied regular-file mode, the configuration/payroll ownership, and the payroll and public-notice text. Keep the public share read-only and available.
steps: Practice on the separate guide server
Repair and verify the full independent assignment
hints: Read the actual failure layer before changing file modes or account policy. A syntax pass is not an access pass.
Use the supplied client identities and id -Gn / ls -ld to distinguish share policy from Unix rights. The public and private resources have their own preservation requirements.
Compare saved versus applied settings and the actual resolved path. Save, apply, then open a new trial; avoid changing an archive to compensate for a wrong destination.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-13: LPIC-2 v4.5 objective209.1; official current Samba smb.conf/testparm manuals identify documentation4.25.0. No local testparm binary was available for a runtime comparison. Bounded standalone policy and existing regular-file text operations only: supplied abstract credential proofs, fixed local Unix identities/groups, enabled SMB records, supported INI directives, saved/applied snapshots and new client trials. Not an SMB/NTLM/Kerberos implementation, real server, AD member, CIFS mount, Windows ACL, printer, NIS, protocol pathname/case-folding, file-creation, locking or open-handle cache model. Paths use exact supplied Unix spelling. Account controls and Apply saved settings are marked simulator administration, not Linux commands. Filesystem terminal subset is listed in optional help. No host filesystem, process, network, service or account is changed.
scenarios.explanation: A named SMB login first needs its enabled supplied account. The mapped Unix user must then traverse the folder and satisfy the regular-file permission checks. The team folder needs group read/search for this task; the already-correct regular-file modes need no broadening. Writer and reviewer policy remains separate from Unix group rights.

scenarios.title: Give writers and reviewers the right share access
scenarios.summary: Apply a share policy that permits team writing and review while preserving a read-only public share.
scenarios.objective: Publish team for mira to read/update the supplied draft and for noor to read while share policy rejects reviewer writes. Reject casey and anonymous connections to the team at authentication/share policy, rather than relying on an inaccessible file. A failed named login must not become guest access. Keep bulletin available for public reads, with a default read-only policy and no write-list exceptions. Preserve supplied regular-file modes, configuration/payroll ownership, and the private and notice contents. Save a supported configuration and apply its policy. The supplied Unix identities, SMB accounts and file inventory remain in place.
steps: Practice on the separate guide server
Repair and verify the full independent assignment
hints: Read the actual failure layer before changing file modes or account policy. A syntax pass is not an access pass.
Use the supplied client identities and id -Gn / ls -ld to distinguish share policy from Unix rights. The public and private resources have their own preservation requirements.
Compare saved versus applied settings and the actual resolved path. Save, apply, then open a new trial; avoid changing an archive to compensate for a wrong destination.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-13: LPIC-2 v4.5 objective209.1; official current Samba smb.conf/testparm manuals identify documentation4.25.0. No local testparm binary was available for a runtime comparison. Bounded standalone policy and existing regular-file text operations only: supplied abstract credential proofs, fixed local Unix identities/groups, enabled SMB records, supported INI directives, saved/applied snapshots and new client trials. Not an SMB/NTLM/Kerberos implementation, real server, AD member, CIFS mount, Windows ACL, printer, NIS, protocol pathname/case-folding, file-creation, locking or open-handle cache model. Paths use exact supplied Unix spelling. Account controls and Apply saved settings are marked simulator administration, not Linux commands. Filesystem terminal subset is listed in optional help. No host filesystem, process, network, service or account is changed.
scenarios.explanation: The team policy must admit the right identities and distinguish write roles before the Unix filesystem is considered. A read-only default plus a writer exception is one supported solution; a writable default plus an explicit reviewer read-list can also meet the team outcomes. The public share still needs its stated read-only default without write exceptions. Guest access and failed named authentication are different cases.

scenarios.title: Handover the correct share without touching archived files
scenarios.summary: Repair a staged-to-production share handover and verify new clients use the intended files.
scenarios.objective: Make new team connections serve /srv/live-team, not /srv/old-team. The writer devon must read/update production files; reviewer imani must read and be denied writes by share policy. Enable the required supplied SMB accounts and restore team listing/search on /srv/live-team. Keep the non-team account and anonymous clients out at authentication/share policy. Keep bulletin available for public reads with its default read-only policy and no write exceptions. Preserve the archived draft, payroll and public-notice text, every supplied regular-file mode, and configuration/payroll ownership. Save and apply the corrected settings, then verify the resolved file paths and outcomes with new client trials. Do not erase archived files or broaden their permissions to make a wrong path work.
steps: Practice on the separate guide server
Repair and verify the full independent assignment
hints: Read the actual failure layer before changing file modes or account policy. A syntax pass is not an access pass.
Use the supplied client identities and id -Gn / ls -ld to distinguish share policy from Unix rights. The public and private resources have their own preservation requirements.
Compare saved versus applied settings and the actual resolved path. Save, apply, then open a new trial; avoid changing an archive to compensate for a wrong destination.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-13: LPIC-2 v4.5 objective209.1; official current Samba smb.conf/testparm manuals identify documentation4.25.0. No local testparm binary was available for a runtime comparison. Bounded standalone policy and existing regular-file text operations only: supplied abstract credential proofs, fixed local Unix identities/groups, enabled SMB records, supported INI directives, saved/applied snapshots and new client trials. Not an SMB/NTLM/Kerberos implementation, real server, AD member, CIFS mount, Windows ACL, printer, NIS, protocol pathname/case-folding, file-creation, locking or open-handle cache model. Paths use exact supplied Unix spelling. Account controls and Apply saved settings are marked simulator administration, not Linux commands. Filesystem terminal subset is listed in optional help. No host filesystem, process, network, service or account is changed.
scenarios.explanation: The handover is complete only when saved supported policy matches applied policy and new client operations reach the production files with the required access. Repointing a share can uncover previously hidden account and directory faults. Verification includes resolved paths, not just matching text or a successful write somewhere. The archive, payroll and public notice remain preserved; public and reviewer writes are denied by share policy.
